Details of Kshethram:
This kshethram comprises two places, Tiruvaali and Tirunagari.  Tiruvaali is said to be the birthplace of Amritavalli Thayaar, and Tirunagari is said to be the birthplace of Lord Vayalali Manavalan.

Tirunagari
Moolavar: Vayalali Manavalan
Thayaar: Amritavalli Thayaar
Vimanam: Ashtakshara Vimanam
Pushkarani: Illakshani Theertham

Tiruvaali
Moolavar: Lakshmi Narasimhar
Thayaar: Amrita Ghatavalli

Travel: Tiruvaali is located 10 km from Sirkazhi, and Tirunagari is located 5 km from Tiruvaali.

Azhwar Pasuram: 
Tirumangai Azhwar: 30 pasuram
Kulasekara Azhwar: 12 pasuram
Total: 42 Pasurams

Sthala Puranam: 
At Tiruvaali, we can see Lakshmi Narasimhar. It is said that after killing Hiranyakashipu, the Lord was still furious. To calm down all the devas, Lord Brahma and Lord Shiva asked Mahalakshmi to isolate the Lord in a different location. Thus, the Lord was taken to Tiruvaali. Usually, we see Lakshmi seated on the Lord’s left lap, but here, she is sitting on the Lord’s right, allowing her to hug and embrace the Lord. Thus, the place got its name Tiruvaali (Tiru meaning "Lakshmi" and Aali meaning "Aalinganam" or "hug" in Sanskrit).
*** Vedupari Utsavam
Tiruvaali is said to be the birthplace of Amritavalli Thayaar, and Tirunagari is said to be the birthplace of Lord Vayalali Manavalan. It is said that on the night that the Lord got married to Thayaar, they were targeted and looted by Tirumangai Azhwar. Before becoming a saint, Tirumangai Azhwar was known as Kaliyan, a dacoit.
Tirumangai Azhwar wanted to marry a woman named Kumudhavalli. She placed two conditions, namely, 1) to get Pancha-Samskaram done, and 2) to perform tadhiyararadhanam (annadhanam) for a thousand people for one year. To satisfy the second condition, Tirumangai Azhwar would often steal gold from anyone he could find and sell it to raise money to serve people. As fate would have it, Tirumangai Azhwar ran into the Lord and Thayaar. He pulled out a knife and told them to remove all the jewelry that they were wearing. The Lord and Thayaar gave up all their jewelry. Tirumangai Azhwar tied up all of the jewelry in a cloth, and as he was about to lift it, the Lord performed an enchantment in such a way that he could no longer lift it. In anger, Tirumangai Azhwar threatened the Lord to give him the mantra that would enable him to lift the bag. The Lord smiled and told him that he was performing all of this to ensure that Tirumangai Azhwar would obtain this mantra and propagate it to the world. Thus, the Lord gave Tirumangai Azhwar the ashtakshara mantram. All of this is performed as a drama to date on Panguni Uttaram day.  Find the pictures of the utsavam attached below.
